dublinCore.description: A to-scale vis-timeline of the nine periods of Eastern Mediterranean history with 29 key events on the trip route, each linked to the chapter that covers it. Learners answer six questions about period lengths and the gaps between events before the relevant bands and events are revealed, then explore every band and event. The appendix companion to the Chapter 1 eras timeline.

topic: Key events on the trip route
learningObjectives: Place key events on the route within the nine periods and compare the time between them, by answering six questions before the answers are revealed, scoring at least 5 of 6
prerequisites: names and order of the nine periods

controls.label: Answer choices
controls.description: Commit one answer per question; one attempt each

controls.label: Next
controls.description: Go to the next question and return to the full span

controls.label: Restart
controls.description: Clear the score, hide the events, and return to question 1
Zoom in, down to a 200-year window

visualElements.description: Nine colored period bands drawn to scale in three staggered rows, with faint full-height shading
Event dots and short spans, revealed as questions are answered; all 29 appear after question 6
Question, feedback with the reason, running score, and an infobox for the selected band or event

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, then check against a to-scale display
keyQuestions: Which lasted longer: the Bronze Age or the Classical period?
Was the Parthenon built closer in time to the first palace at Knossos or to Paul's years in Ephesus?
Which lasted longer: the Byzantine period or the Ottoman period?
Did Paul teach in Ephesus before or during the Pax Romana?
How many years passed between 480 BCE and 330 CE?
In which period was writing almost unknown in Greece?
commonMisconceptions: The Classical period was long because it is famous
The Byzantine period was a short epilogue to Rome
Spans across the BCE/CE line are found by subtracting the two numbers
Writing in Greece was continuous from the Bronze Age onward
assessmentOpportunities: Six multiple-choice questions, one attempt each; mastery is 5 of 6 on the first attempt
